stemMd: The average waiting time at a clinic is lower than at any nearby clinic. Its manager concludes that every patient waits less there than any patient waits at the other clinics. The conclusion improperly

options.label: A
options.textMd: infers a cause from a single correlation.

options.label: B
options.textMd: takes a recommendation as evidence of a fact.

options.label: D
options.textMd: extends a comparison of averages to every individual observation.

options.label: E
options.textMd: compares waiting time with treatment time.

explanationMd: An average summarizes a distribution and can conceal overlap. Some patients at the lowest-average clinic may still wait longer than some patients elsewhere. A comparison of means cannot justify the universal claim.

distractorRationale.c: Preferences play no role in the numerical inference.
distractorRationale.a: The conclusion is universal, not causal.
